summary: Skill front matter: name, long self-description claiming unmatched breadth, stack coverage list, keyword triggers, a list of enforced absolutes, and a title banner.
Persona block casting the reader as four adversarial reviewer roles with per-role veto lists, plus a list of industry standards treated as a compliance floor with thresholds.
mech: Before release, review through four lenses (design, security, delivery weight, data); any listed veto item found blocks release until fixed and rechecked.

Security/data vetoes: read-then-write races, missing rate limits, CSRF or CSP gaps, ownership-check holes, client-trusted decisions, tokens in web storage, unvalidated webhooks, unindexed or unbounded queries, wildcard rules.

Design/delivery vetoes: contrast below 4.5:1, touch target below 44px, animation without stated curve, unjustified bundle growth above 20KB gzip, heavy dependency lacking justification (source figures).

summary: Sixteen-step hidden pre-output protocol: classification, decomposition, token and threat pre-audits, performance budget, concurrency plan, conflict hierarchy, anti-truncation pledge, architecture, defense, testing, observability, AI, fixed-style check, standards declaration.
mech: Before writing, classify the deliverable and list every section, state, edge case, route, rule and test it needs; at the end confirm each listed item is present.

Resolve requirement conflicts in fixed order: explicit user instruction, security, performance budget, accessibility floor, house style, platform guidance, tokens, general practice; state each resolution.
For every input, write and external call name the attack vector and its defense; steps that do not apply are marked not-applicable with a written reason.

summary: Section banner announcing thirty absolute laws and stating that any violation means full output rejection.

Table demanding exact machine-readable formats for dimensions, timing, easing, springs, haptics, spacing, radius, weight, opacity, layering, targets, blur, contrast, budgets, cache, rate limits, concurrency; vague words forbidden.
mech: When a spec states size, timing, easing, opacity, layer order, contrast, cache time, rate limit or load target, give an exact value with unit.
Review scan: flag vague adjectives such as fast, large, rounded, readable, scalable, reasonable; replace each with a measured value or mark it unknown.

summary: Ban on raw color literals in any language plus a mandated named token set: surfaces, brand, status, text, borders, shadows, overlays, presence, spacing, radius, type, motion, layers, including product-themed tokens.
mech: Reference color only through role-named tokens (surface, text, border, status, on-color pairs) so theme and contrast are changed and audited in one place; grep for raw literals.
Use closed scales for spacing (4px grid), radius, motion duration and layer order; an off-scale value needs a stated reason, preventing magic numbers and stacking bugs.
Layer scale names each stacking level in ascending order (base, raised, floating nav, dropdown, sticky, overlay, modal, notification, tooltip, command palette); pick levels by name, never ad hoc.

summary: Rule forbidding ellipses, placeholders, TODO markers and cross-references in place of content; every list, file, state and error path must be written out regardless of length.
mech: Before delivery, search the output for placeholder markers (ellipsis, TODO, bracketed stubs, same-as-above phrases); complete each hit or declare it explicitly out of scope.

summary: State matrix template for every interactive component: nineteen listed states (heading says eighteen) with columns for visual change, haptic and animation, plus appended domain states.
mech: For each interactive component fill a state table: idle, hover, keyboard focus, press-in, release, long-press, drag, loading, success, error, warning, disabled, empty, skeleton, offline/stale, plus domain states.
Each state row records visual change in tokens and dimensions, haptic type and timing or none, animation curve and duration or none; blank cells fail review.
Situational rows in the source: streaming output, live-update pulse, rate-throttled, banned; disabled uses dedicated tokens instead of reduced opacity.

summary: Seven-part record template required for every gesture: trigger, haptic, animation phases, visual feedback, performance path, state result, and an abuse-detection behavior signal.
mech: Per gesture record trigger (type, threshold, target size, debounce), haptic (type, timing, platform), animation phases (property, range, duration, easing), visual feedback with reduced-motion fallback.
Also record render path and state result: final UI state, navigation effect, API call marked optimistic or confirmed, store mutation; verify by walking the interaction end to end.
Seventh part logs the interaction as an abuse signal with risk weight and throttle hook; apply only on security-sensitive surfaces.

summary: Accessibility requirements per component: target sizes, contrast ratios, focus indicators, ARIA attributes, keyboard map, reduced-motion wrappers, live-region announcements, color independence, focus management.
mech: Check targets at least 44x44px (48dp Android), body contrast 4.5:1, large text 3:1, and a visible 2px offset focus ring never removed without replacement.
Keyboard pass: Tab reaches every control, Enter or Space activates, Escape dismisses, arrows move within lists; dialog open focuses first element, close returns focus to trigger.
Async changes announce through a live region; status never by color alone; every animation has a reduced-motion alternative; input errors linked by description attributes.

summary: Table of mandatory performance comments classifying animations, images, fonts, data fetches and realtime operations by render path and cost, mostly in one framework's vocabulary.
mech: Classify each animation by render path: transform and opacity run on the compositor; height, background and shadow changes trigger layout or repaint and should be avoided or limited.
Mark the above-fold image as the largest-paint candidate and prioritize it; blur effects need a low-end device test; prefer server-side fetch over client waterfalls.

summary: Security law with code templates: atomic concurrency options, validated handler order, value-creation tracing with audit entries, least-privilege database rules, six rate-limit profiles, security headers, prompt-injection handling, object-ownership checks.
mech: Handler order: authenticate server-side, rate-limit per user and action class, parse safely, validate with a strict schema rejecting unknown keys, then run logic; test each rejection status.
Shared balances or counters change only inside an atomic transaction or server function; separate read-then-write is a finding; each change writes an immutable before/after audit entry.
Check ownership on every client-supplied id and answer not-found on mismatch; keep untrusted text in the user role inside delimiters; schema-validate model output.

summary: Framework-specific architecture rules: server-versus-client component decision table, cache and revalidation settings, utility-class discipline forbidding arbitrary pixel values, and a skeleton shimmer snippet with reduced-motion fallback.
mech: Default to server rendering; move a component client-side only for local state, effects, event handlers, browser APIs, realtime subscriptions or canvas and charts; record the split.
Use the utility scale instead of arbitrary pixel values; arbitrary syntax is allowed only to reference a design token.
Put dynamic regions behind a loading boundary with a content-shaped skeleton; the shimmer loop needs a static reduced-motion fallback.

summary: Typed-language strictness rules: forbidden patterns (untyped values, unguarded assertions, casts on external data, magic values) and required patterns (discriminated unions, schema-inferred types, safe catch, named constants, strict compiler flags).
mech: Model async state as a discriminated union (idle, loading, success, error with retryable flag, plus domain states) so each UI state must be handled.
Never cast external data to a type; parse it with a schema and infer the type; catch errors as unknown and narrow before use.
Ban untyped escape hatches, unguarded non-null assertions and magic numbers; name constants; enable strict compiler flags including unchecked-index and exact-optional checks.

summary: Code template for a streaming LLM endpoint: session check, per-user rate limit, schema-validated message list, static system prompt, sanitized user content, fixed output cap, event-stream response.
mech: LLM endpoint order: authenticate, rate-limit per user, schema-validate messages (roles, per-message length cap, count cap), static system prompt, capped output tokens, streamed response.
Audit caution: the template accepts client-supplied assistant turns and hard-codes a model id; check for history forgery and stale ids when reusing.

summary: Offline and installable-web-app notes: cache strategy per resource class, manifest icon sizes, optimistic UI with sync on reconnect, and a network-status hook example.
mech: Choose cache strategy per resource class: cache-first for static assets, network-first for API, stale-while-revalidate for content, background sync for queued mutations.
Show offline writes as pending and sync on reconnect; drive an offline indicator from connectivity events, verified by toggling the network.

summary: Testing template with stubbed bodies: schema unit tests, handler integration tests per status code, two end-to-end flows, load-test thresholds, and a large concurrent-user abuse simulation.
mech: For each server handler write one test per rejection path (unauthenticated, banned, rate-limited, invalid payload, business-rule failure) plus a success test asserting the side effect.
Schema unit tests cover negative, over-maximum, unknown-field and valid inputs; end-to-end covers the main flow and one graceful-failure flow.
State load thresholds numerically (source: p95 under 500ms, failure rate under 1%); the 10K-user, 1K-attacker simulation is a source claim needing real tooling.

summary: Observability snippets: error tracker setup that strips personal fields, a structured JSON logger with a security level, and analytics funnel event examples.
mech: Strip email and IP from error reports before sending; log structured JSON with level, message and timestamp; keep a separate security-event level.
Instrument funnel start, completion and failure with reason codes; hash user identifiers in analytics events.

summary: Single-job continuous-integration workflow template: install, type-check, lint, unit, integration, build, end-to-end, stress, security suite, then a page-performance audit.
mech: Gate order on every push and pull request: clean install, type-check, lint, unit, integration, build, end-to-end, performance audit; any failing step blocks merge.

summary: Environment schema example validating server-only and public variables at startup, plus a ban on admin keys in the repository and payment secrets in the client bundle.
mech: Validate all environment variables against a schema at startup and fail fast; keep server-only secrets apart from public-prefixed values.
Audit: no service-account key in the repository and no payment secret in client code; verify by searching history and built assets for key names.

summary: Client data-layer example tied to two named libraries: an optimistic mutation that snapshots, applies, rolls back on error and refetches on settle.
mech: Optimistic update: cancel in-flight reads, snapshot the previous value, apply the change, restore the snapshot on error, refetch on settle.
Caution: the example applies optimism to a monetary balance; confirm-first is safer for financial values.

summary: Internationalization rule tied to one library: no hard-coded strings, one complete message file per locale, locale detection in middleware, locale-aware date, number and currency formatting.
mech: No user-facing string literal in markup; copy comes from message keys with complete per-locale files; dates, numbers and currency use locale-aware formatting.

summary: Token change-log template: change type, old and new token name, reason, migration command, breaking flag and affected components.
mech: Each design-token change records type (added, deprecated, renamed, removed), old and new name, one-line reason, migration command, breaking flag and affected components.

summary: Documentation-comment example for a public function: purpose, parameters with constraints, thrown errors, return value and a security note.
mech: Public functions carry a doc block: purpose, each parameter with constraints, each thrown error with its condition, return value, and security notes (auth, rate limit, audit).
